newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO cites pressure from Japanese.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO cites pressure from Japanese.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chairman Robert Eaton said the automaker managed to increase its first quarter earnings despite stiff competition from Japanese automakers.

"Competition for the consumer's automotive dollar got increasingly intense in the first quarter," Eaton said in a statement accompanying Chrysler's earnings results for the period. "At the same time, the combination of a weak yen and new entries from Japan put considerable pressure on all of the domestic manufacturers while giving Japanese automakers an opportunity to increase their exports to the U.S. market."

Chrysler, offsetting higher incentive spending with stronger production volume, reported first quarter earnings of $1.029 billion, or $1.45 per fully diluted common share, up about 2.4 percent from year-earlier profits of $1.005 billion, or $1.30 a share.

The automaker also said it repurchased $587 million worth of common stock during the period as part of its plan to repurchase $2 billion in common stock for all of 1997. Since the beginning of 1995, Chrysler has bought back $3.7 billion worth of stock.

"We're optimistic as we enter the Spring selling season and as we continue to maintain our U.S. industry sales forecast for the 1997 calendar year at 15 million to 15.5 million units, assuming the economy holds and interest rates don't increase substantially," he added.
Despite the earnings gain, Chrysler's net earnings as a total percent of revenues during the first quarter fell to 6.4 percent, compared to 6.7 percent a year ago.
Eaton noted that cost cutting efforts from suppliers, which resulted in $1 billion worth of new savings ideas in 1996, are continuing.

"We recognize that 'good enough' isn't good enough in any business today," he said. "We know we simply have to do more and more things better every single day to keep ahead fo the market. That's our focus for 1997 and beyond.
